config_writers: firewall.sh: #Set a flag to allow mini-igd to append firewall rule
firewall.sh: #echo "Clean conntrack table first before Re-Set Iptables Rules"
firewall.sh: #if opmode is bridge , exit don't set firewall
firewall.sh: #iptables -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss $MTU
firewall.sh: iptables  -A FORWARD -i $WAN -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
firewall.sh: iptables -A FORWARD -i $WAN -p udp -m udp --destination  224.0.0.0/4 -j ACCEPT
firewall.sh: iptables -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
firewall.sh: iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
firewall.sh: iptables -A INPUT -p icmp --icmp-type echo-request -i $WAN -d $EXT_IP -j ACCEPT
firewall.sh: iptables -A INPUT -p icmp --icmp-type echo-request -i $WAN -d $EXT_IP -j DROP
firewall.sh: iptables -A PREROUTING -t nat -p ALL -d $EXT_IP -j DNAT --to $DMZ_HOST
firewall.sh: iptables -A PREROUTING -t nat -p TCP --dport $port1:$port2 -d $EXT_IP -j DNAT --to $ip
firewall.sh: iptables -A PREROUTING -t nat -p UDP --dport $port1:$port2 -d $EXT_IP -j DNAT --to $ip
notes: Evidence levels: L0 route/string present, L1 parameters identified, L2 dangerous sink present in firmware, L3 route/parameter-to-sink flow should be proven with decompiler, L4 filter bypass plausible, L5 live PoC confirmed.
This triage increases zero-day coverage but does not replace route-specific reverse engineering or live emulation.
